title: Sunny Finds Her Favourite Spot | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka walks all her familiar paths one after another and finally realises that her favourite spot in the whole bush has been the same small patch of soft grass by the creek all along. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
Sunny walked all her usual paths.

The creek path. The path through the wattles. The path past the old hollow gum. The high path that gave her a view of the valley. The low path with the soft moss along the edges.

She walked them all, slowly, in the moonlight.

At each one she stopped and thought: is this it? Is this my favourite?

The creek path was beautiful. The wattle path smelled wonderful. The hollow gum path felt ancient and important. The high path gave her the stars. The mossy path was the softest.

She couldn't decide.

She walked back to the beginning — back to the place where the creek bank widened slightly and there was a patch of soft grass under a single paperback tree, with the water sound close and the moonlight reaching all the way down through the canopy.

She stopped.

She had been here a hundred times before. Maybe more. She had always just passed through.

She sat down in the soft grass.

The creek moved past. The moonlight fell exactly right. The paperbark tree creaked gently.

This was it.

This had always been it. She had just been too busy walking past to notice.

She settled deeper into the grass.

Some places take a long time to be found, even if you have already been there.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, favourite spot. Goodnight, little one.
